target.name: Mons Mouton (lunar south pole)
target.description: A lunar south-pole region NASA listed among its Artemis III landing candidates in 2024. NASA now describes Artemis III as a crewed demonstration in low Earth orbit (launch 2027), with lunar landings beginning with Artemis IV.

descriptionSources.name: NASA (2024): update to 9 Artemis III landing regions

ndvi.source: no vegetation (by definition)

albedo.source: estimate: broadband albedo = 0.49 x LOLA 1064 nm normal albedo (Hayne et al. 2017, doi:10.1002/2017JE005387) with typical highland normal albedo ~0.3 (Lucey et al. 2014, doi:10.1002/2013JE004592); not a site-specific measurement

precip.source: airless body

sun_max_deg.source: computed: 90 - (84.6 - 1.54); lunar equator tilt to the ecliptic 1.54 deg (Cassini state); terrain and summit height ignored

volcanic.source: not applicable: the rule describes the Earth campaign terrain, not the target (see breaks)

variables.label: Vegetation (NDVI)
variables.why: EVA analogs need bare rock; target has none

variables.label: Surface albedo
variables.why: dark ground like lunar regolith (broadband ~0.15, estimate)

variables.label: Precipitation
variables.why: arid ground stays bare and unweathered

variables.label: Basic volcanic rock nearby (GLiM)
variables.why: the EVA campaigns ran on basalt lava fields

variables.label: Highest noon Sun elevation in the year
variables.why: south-pole EVAs work under a Sun always near the horizon (JETT3/5 used a 'sun cart')

variables.label: Noon Sun elevation at winter solstice
Slope
variables.why: walkable terrain; needs Copernicus DEM 30 m (not available tonight)

breaks.text: Gravity: 1.62 m/s2 on the Moon vs 9.80 on Earth (0.165 g); suits, walking and sampling loads differ.
Vacuum: lunar surface pressure ~3e-15 bar (night) vs 1014 mb on Earth; no air for cooling or to slow dust.
breaks.source: NASA NSSDC Moon and Earth fact sheets

breaks.text: Lighting: at Mons Mouton the Sun stays below ~7 deg (computed from latitude 84.6 S and the 1.54 deg tilt of the lunar equator to the ecliptic); low-latitude Earth sites see it near overhead.
Rock: the lunar south pole is highland terrain with anorthosite (feldspar-rich rock), not mare basalt; basalt sites train EVA operations, not target composition.
breaks.source: NASA JSC, Houston We Have a Podcast ep. 236 (D. Kring, LPI)

validation.method: similarity = 0.5 x rule fraction + 0.5 x (1 - percentile distance to the known-analog median); every 0.1 deg land cell scored; percentile of each known analog among all land cells; Amazonia as negative control.
validation.result: 3 of 4 known analogs in the top 2 % of land cells (SP Crater 99.9, Craters of the Moon 98.6, Timanfaya 99.6); Kilauea Iki 86.4 (11 km cell mostly rainforest). Amazonia control: 31.2th percentile.

sand.source: no comparable measurement found; scored against mission need (loose sand), not a Mars value

ndvi.source: no vegetation

precip.source: no liquid precipitation

breaks.text: Gravity: 3.73 m/s2 on Mars (0.38 g); a rover weighs ~2.6x more on Earth, so sinkage differs unless mass is reduced (JPL's Scarecrow).

breaks.text: Atmosphere: 6.36 mb mean surface pressure on Mars vs 1014 mb on Earth; wind moves sand differently.

lst_mean.source: annual and diurnal mean surface temperature (197 K) at 46.7N, 192E, Mars Climate Database v6.2 (climatology, average solar scenario; all Ls in 15 deg steps, all local times, equal Ls weighting); Mars Climate Database (c) LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES. Model value

precip.source: no liquid precipitation

albedo.source: MGS TES bolometric (Lambert) albedo, 8 ppd global map, mean of 47-49N/188-192E (Christensen et al. 2001, doi:10.1029/2000JE001370; PDS GLOBAL_ALBEDO_8PPD)

ndvi.source: no vegetation

ice.source: SWIM ice-consistency map exists (1/20 deg GeoTIFF) but server was down on 2026-11-14

variables.label: Mean surface temperature
variables.why: ground ice persists where the mean is below freezing (permafrost proxy)

variables.label: Precipitation
variables.why: polar desert: ice in the ground, not snow on top

variables.label: Surface albedo
variables.why: excludes ice sheets and glaciers (~0.8); Arcadia is dark ground (TES albedo ~0.23) over ice

breaks.text: Low pressure (6.36 mb): on Mars drilled ice sublimes instead of melting and refreezing on the bit, unlike Earth permafrost.
breaks.source: NASA NSSDC Mars fact sheet; Honeybee chamber tests (phys.org 2010)

breaks.text: Temperature: Mars average ~-59 C; Arcadia annual mean about -76 C (Mars Climate Database); the Earth sites in this mission have 2024 mean surface temperatures of about -13 to -29 C (MODIS) and a summer thaw layer.
breaks.source: NASA NSSDC Mars fact sheet; Mars Climate Database v6.2 (http://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mcd_python/); MODIS 2024 (this dataset)

breaks.text: Gravity 0.38 g and no liquid precipitation on Mars; Earth polar deserts still get snow.
